markets.rules_secondary:
“Dropped out” means any of the following:
Max Miller announces they are ending, suspending, or withdrawing from their campaign
Max Miller files official withdrawal paperwork with relevant election authorities
Max Miller publicly states they are no longer seeking the office
Max Miller endorses another candidate while stating they are no longer running
Max Miller is disqualified by election authorities or courts and does not appeal

The following do NOT constitute dropping out:
Losing a primary or election
Failing to qualify for debates or ballots
Temporarily suspending campaign activities without withdrawing
Being eliminated through the normal election process
Reducing campaign activities while remaining a candidate

Key provisions:
Once someone drops out per above criteria, the market resolves YES even if they later re-enter
“Suspending” a campaign is treated as dropping out unless Max Miller explicitly states they remain a candidate
For primary races, dropping out of the presidential race entirely counts as dropping out of that party’s primary
Withdrawing from the race counts even if the person remains on the ballot

markets.rules_primary: If the Senate has conducted any recorded vote on the CLARITY Act after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This includes:
Roll call votes
Recorded votes
Yea-and-nay votes
Electronic votes (in the House)
Division/standing votes

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Voice votes where individual member positions are not recorded
Unanimous consent agreements without a recorded vote
Votes in committee, unless the bill/motion specifically refers to a committee vote
Procedural determinations by the presiding officer
Deemed passage without an actual vote

For clarity:
A vote on cloture regarding the bill/motion, including cloture on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion, DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on the rule governing debate of the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion if the bill/motion specifically refers to that rule
A vote on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on final passage DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on an amendment to the bill/motion does NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion unless the bill/motion specifically refers to that amendment
markets.title: Will the Senate vote on CLARITY Act?

No contracts pay $1 minus the Yes payout.
If the league officially uses a tiebreaker to determine a single leader, the market resolves based on the league's official winner.
